newsitem.title: USA: Santander says Brazil debt undervalued.
newsitem.headline: Santander says Brazil debt undervalued.

text.p: Brazil's debt is relatively undervalued, while Mexico's and Venezuela's debt prices have already anticipated fundamental improvements, said Santander Investment in its latest report on sovereign risk.

Santander derived its relative ranking from its proprietary Income-Base Credit Model, which measures affordability of external debt, credibitlity of economic policy, sustainability of a favorable capital flow environment, and institutional factors.

While uncertainty over Brazil's trade deficit, constitutional amendments allowing presidential reelection and the privatilization of CVRD is unlikely to be resolved in two to three months, the outlook may turn more positive by late January, it said.

Compared with Brazil, Argentina mainstains a slight edge on the economic fundamentals because its recovery is less likely to lead to overheating, but the debt prices are less attractive, according to the report.

Political and economic improvements notwithstanding, Mexico's huge ambition to roll over maturing debt next year may create supply pressure, while Venezuela is faced with rising interest rates when the government drains liquidity from the rising oil revenues, it continued.
Among non-Latin debts, the Santander report considered both Poland and Russia "fairly valued."
